chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abī Wallād, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: What do you think about a man who holds office in the service of the sulṭān, having no livelihood except from their works? I pass by him and stay with him, and he hosts me and treats me kindly, and sometimes he orders dirhams and clothing to be given to me, and my chest has become constricted because of that.
So he said to me: Take it and eat from it; the benefit is for you, and the burden of sin is upon him.

key_terms.أَعْمَالَ السُّلْطَانِ: service and administrative work under the ruling authority
key_terms.الْكِسْوَةِ: clothing given as provision or gift
key_terms.الْمَهْنَأُ: the lawful enjoyment or benefit received
key_terms.فَيُضِيفُنِي: he hosts me as a guest

ai.seo_question: Can a person accept gifts or hospitality from someone employed by the sulṭān if his income is doubtful?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses receiving hospitality or gifts from someone whose income comes from serving the ruling authority. Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام states that the recipient may take and benefit from it, while the sin rests upon the one responsible for the wrongful source. It is significant in discussions of livelihood, doubtful earnings, and legal responsibility.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3662 - Al-Hasan bin Mahbub narrate from Abu Walad who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (as), 'What do you think about a man who holds positions in the service of the Sultan and has no means of livelihood except through his work for them?
I pass by him, and he hosts me, treats me kindly, and sometimes gives me dirhams and clothing. I feel uneasy about this.'
Imam (as) said to me: 'Take it and eat from it, for the benefit is yours, and the sin is upon him.'
